fact: Artifact attestations establish provenance and integrity guarantees for build artifacts, so consumers can verify where and how software was built.
Attestations include workflow, repository, organization, environment, commit SHA, triggering event, and OIDC-related information.
GitHub says artifact attestations by themselves provide SLSA v1.0 Build Level 2; reusable workflows can help meet Build Level 3.
Binary artifact attestation needs id-token: write, contents: read, attestations: write, and uses actions/attest@v4 with subject-path.
GitHub CLI verifies binary artifact attestations with gh attestation verify PATH -R OWNER/REPO.
GitHub warns that artifact attestations do not guarantee an artifact is secure; consumers still need policy and risk decisions.
On GitHub Free, Pro, and Team plans, artifact attestations are available for public repositories; private/internal repositories require Enterprise Cloud.
SLSA v1.2 was announced on 2025-11-24 and introduced the Source Track for source authoring, review, and management threats.
PyPI implements PEP 740 digital attestations and accepts SLSA Provenance and PyPI Publish attestations.
PEP 740 standardizes index support for digitally signed attestations and provenance objects for Python package distributions.
Cosign bundles include signature, certificate, timestamp, and transparency log inclusion proof.
